# QUICK START — Day One

**AI Chief of Staff, v1.3.0. Created by The NoW of Work.**

Someone has already installed this for you. They followed `READ-ME-FIRST.md`. Ten minutes here and you can use it.

**It drafts. It never sends.** It will write a reply, a brief, or a draft of `tomorrow.md` without being asked, and it keeps `connections.md` current itself. Nothing leaves the workspace. No email goes out, no calendar moves, no reply is posted, and `tomorrow.md` is never saved until you say yes. If it offers to connect a tool or sign you in, that is a defect. It cannot authenticate anything.

---

## What you can say

Say it in your own words. There are fourteen behaviours. Six of them carry the week.

| When you want | Say |
|---|---|
| Setup, first time or again | "Run onboarding." |
| What today needs from you | "Run the morning brief." |
| The inbox cut down to what needs a person | "Triage my inbox." |
| To walk into a meeting ready | "Prep me for the 2:00 with Priya." |
| The day closed out | "Close out the day." |
| The week before it starts | "Run the weekly review." |

The other seven wait for a situation, and you learn each one when its situation arrives. Say "Turn this into actions" when a meeting just ended and the decisions are still only in your head, "Sweep yesterday's meetings" when recorded calls have stacked up, "Chase what I'm owed" when people have gone quiet, "Brief me on the pricing decision" when a call is due and you want the options and a recommendation, "What did we decide about the lease?" when the answer is somewhere in your own record and you want the source, "Run a connection check" when the output has gone thin and you suspect a tool has dropped, and "Check the setup" when something is off and you want the whole workspace audited in fix order.

Five of those seven also arrive on their own once the schedule is set. Saying the phrase runs one now rather than waiting for it.

---

## The files you own

- `about-me.md` — who you are, how you work, and who you can never miss.
- `my-work.md` — what this quarter is for, and what you have left alone.
- `tomorrow.md` — your intent for the next working day. That day, it outranks every other file you own.
- `commitments.md` — open promises, yours and other people's.
- `decisions.md` — choices you actually closed, and what would change your mind about each one. It drafts entries after you decide. It never writes an outcome you have not stated.
- `connections.md` — not yours. It records what the system can reach, so it can tell a quiet week from a broken connector. Leave it alone.

If you are running this in ChatGPT, it writes through a connected app such as Google Drive and asks before each write, and where nothing is connected it prints the file in a code block for you to save.

Onboarding takes ten minutes. Give it twenty more on four answers: `about-me.md` section 6 (who you can never miss) and section 8 (hard stops), `my-work.md` section 1 (what this quarter is for) and section 5 (what you are not doing). Spend longest on section 5, and treat anything still in `[BRACKETS]` as a decision nobody has made yet.

---

## What a brief looks like

```
Today is about getting the Q3 pricing memo signed before the board pack closes.

PRIORITIES
1. Sign off the Q3 pricing memo. Finance needs it before Thursday's board
   pack. (source: my-work.md section 2)
2. Priya Anand has waited nine days on the supply contract and has asked
   twice. (source: commitments.md)
3. The warehouse lease can wait. Nothing external moves on it until Friday.

CALENDAR
  14:00  Ridley renewal. No agenda on file, and the last one ended on a
         number nobody wrote down. (uncertain)

OPEN LOOPS
  Priya Anand, supply contract, awaiting 9 days.
  Sven Lindquist, warehouse lease redline, due tomorrow.

DRAFTS WAITING
  Reply to Priya on the contract timeline. briefs/2026-03-04-draft-priya.md
```

That is 109 words. Sections with nothing in them do not render at all. The cap is 400 words, and when it runs long it cuts the capability line first and the priorities never.

Your first one will be shorter than this. `commitments.md` starts empty, so there are no open loops yet, and nothing has drafted a reply for you. Expect the opening line and two or three priorities. Loops and drafts arrive once inbox triage is running and the ledger has a week in it. Nothing about connections on day one either. Silence there means it is working. Later on, connections do get a line, in three cases only: you connect a tool and it asks once whether to switch a behaviour on, a connected tool has quietly stopped returning anything, or it names a tool you do not have that would have caught something specific yesterday. One line at most. It still cannot connect or sign in to anything itself.

---

## The one habit worth building

When the brief gets something wrong, correct the file it came from.

| It got this wrong | Fix this |
|---|---|
| A name, a title, a term | `about-me.md` section 5 |
| The tone of a draft | `about-me.md` section 3 |
| Which priority leads | `my-work.md` section 2 |
| Someone it should not have buried | `about-me.md` section 6 |

Editing the output fixes one morning. Editing the file fixes every morning after it.
